incidents-bot: Pager alert -> high_token_count: tenant=zenturi (VPC-dedicated-pool-7)
incidents-bot: severity=high, symptom=token_count_per_min spike -> 18x baseline, quota_exceeded=true, billing_alert=true
incidents-bot: page sent to @james_oncall and @eli_sre at 2026-03-15T10:00:34Z

james_oncall: I'm on it. grabbing logs from the dedicated pool now. any customer-facing impact reported?
maria_support: Customer (Zenturi) emailed CSM, says they saw a huge billing jump and started getting 429s for quota. They want immediate mitigation and a timeline.

james_oncall: ok -- initial grep: 
```
2026-03-15T09:59:12Z tenant=zenturi req_id=abc123 tokens_reported=18345 model=gptx-3.8 variant=quant4
2026-03-15T09:59:13Z tenant=zenturi req_id=abc124 tokens_reported=18299 model=gptx-3.8 variant=quant4
2026-03-15T09:59:15Z tenant=zenturi req_id=abc125 tokens_reported=17900 model=gptx-3.8 variant=quant4
```
These look ~18k tokens for requests that historically were ~1k. suspicious.

tom_engineer: can you paste the raw input bytes for one of the affected requests (req_id=abc123)? trying to repro tokenizer mismatch.
james_oncall: pulling from VPC gateway logs, got base64 payload: `SGVsbG8g8J+YgA==` (appears to contain non-UTF8 sequence). decoding as utf-8 yields replacement chars.

eli_sre: this smells like an encoding mismatch at customer side - they're probably sending UTF-16LE or escaped surrogate pairs which our tokenizer is treating as many tokens. we saw similar with another customer but different root cause.

customer-eng-zenturi: Confirming our SDK had a recent change. We shipped a Java client that uses Java's "String.getBytes()" without specifying charset; some environments default to UTF-16LE. We're investigating.

maria_support: customer asks for immediate steps: 1) stop additional charges, 2) reduce token consumption, 3) restore service so users aren't 429'd.

james_oncall: immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) place tenant on temporary throttled policy to cap tokens/request to 2k; 2) enable request-level normalization at proxy to force interpreting body bytes as UTF-8 and replace non-decodable sequences with safe placeholder; 3) route tenant to fallback model variant with tokenizer that behaves more predictably for malformed input. which of these do we have safe automation for?

tom_engineer: we have a runtime flag `--force-utf8-normalize` on the VPC gateway but it's behind a ticket and not toggled in prod for safety. can flip it for a single tenant with `gwctl set-tenant --id zenturi --force-utf8-normalize true` (dev tested).

james_oncall: do it. also put a per-tenant cap with `admin-api` so we stop billing explosion:
```
POST /internal/admin/tenants/zenturi/policy
{ "max_tokens_per_request": 2000, "billing_override": "suspend_overage_charges" }
```

eli_sre: I'll run the gateway flag and monitor for regressions, james please apply admin-api cap.
james_oncall: applying cap now... 
```
HTTP 200 { "tenant": "zenturi", "max_tokens_per_request": 2000, "billing_override": "suspend_overage_charges" }
```

incidents-bot: action record created -> incident/1789001234, automations: throttle_applied, billing_hold_requested

tom_engineer: gateway flag toggled for tenant zenturi: `gwctl` returned OK. pushing small restart to pick up normalization change.

eli_sre: watching metrics: token_count spike drops from 18x -> 1.4x baseline after normalization. request latency up ~30ms, acceptable.
maria_support: customer notified via email: we applied temporary cap + normalization; billing team notified to hold charges while we investigate. they replied: "thank you, please confirm once you have root cause and ETA for permanent fix."

james_oncall: next steps: 1) coordinate with Zenturi eng to push client fix (explicit UTF-8 encoding in SDK) 2) schedule a job to retroactively re-tokenize affected payloads for billing reconciliation 3) decide whether to keep gateway normalization or require client fix.

customer-eng-zenturi: SDK PR ready, will roll patch to prod in ~90 minutes across their fleet. They also want us to preserve raw input for 24h so they can validate.

billing-bot: Created billing ticket BILL-5982, status=on_hold, linked_incident=1789001234, owner=billing-team

eli_sre: handoff to @eli_sre for night coverage at 2026-03-15T11:30:00Z. current status: mitigation applied (throttle + normalization), customer patch incoming, billing hold in place, monitoring for token regressions. open tasks: a) run retro-billing reconciliation for ~3k affected requests, b) prepare rollback plan for gateway normalization if it causes downstream issues, c) follow up on quota resets.

james_oncall: all noted. I'll add runbook entries to incident page and leave a short summary for the handoff.

james_oncall: HANDOFF SUMMARY: incident 1789001234 -> tenant zenturi. root cause: customer SDK sending UTF-16LE/unspecified-charset strings causing tokenizer to fragment into surrogate tokens; mitigation: gateway-level utf8 normalization + per-tenant token cap + billing hold; customer patch ETA ~90m; outstanding: billing reconciliation + persist raw payloads 24h + decide permanent enforcement (client fix vs gateway normalization).

eli_sre: taking it. ping me if anything spikes. I'll keep the thread updated. :handshake:

maria_support: I'll keep customer comms updated and request evidence for credit once billing completes reconciliation.

incidents-bot: incident 1789001234 transitioned to MONITORED state.

eli_sre: quick note for postmortem: include timeline, SDK diff, sample raw payload (redacted), and the cost impact estimate. i'll own the follow-ups with customer-eng and billing.

customer-eng-zenturi: Thanks everyone. We'll push the SDK patch and post back here once done. appreciate the quick response.

eli_sre: last update before wrap: gateway normalization looks stable; token_count back to baseline as of 2026-03-15T11:15:00Z. keeping billing hold until reconciliation is complete.

incidents-bot: incident 1789001234 marked RESOLVED by eli_sre at 2026-03-15T12:01:18Z (monitoring window passed).
